newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH NEW CAR SALES ROSE SIX PERCENT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH NEW CAR SALES ROSE SIX PERCENT IN 1996.

text.p: New car sales in The Netherlands rose by six percent to 473,474 in 1996, Dutch automotive body (RAI) said on Wednesday.
RAI said last year's growth was driven mainly by higher consumer spending and low interest rates.
This year, RAI expects consumer spending to level off, with new car sales dipping a touch to between 465,000 and 470,000.
Last year's best sellers were again General Motors , with 64,763 cars, or 13.67 percent of total new sales.
Volkswagen/Audi kept up the pressure, with 1996 sales of 64,133, or 13.54 percent, versus 57,452 in 1995.
